problems.title: Arrangements divided by combinations
problems.question: Find A(199,4)/C(199,4).
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a counting formula, identity, or geometric model.
steps: Cancel the common factors. The quotient is 4!=24.

problems.title: Exactly twelve diamonds
problems.question: A52-card deck has 13 diamonds. Find the probability that13 selected cards contain exactly 12 diamonds.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a counting formula, identity, or geometric model.
steps: Choose12 of the 13 diamonds and 1 of the 39 other cards. Divide by the number of equally likely13-card subsets.

problems.title: Add two inequalities
problems.question: Maximize x+y subject to 2x+3y≤10 and 3x+2y≤10.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a counting formula, identity, or geometric model.
formulas: Adding gives 5(x+y)≤20.
steps: Thus x+y≤4. Equality is attained at x=y=2, which satisfies both constraints.

problems.title: Reflection in the vertical axis
problems.question: Reflect y=(x−1)²+1 in the y-axis.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a counting formula, identity, or geometric model.
formulas: Reflection replaces x by −x.
steps: The image is y=(−x−1)²+1=(x+1)²+1.

problems.title: A trapezoid vector
problems.question: In trapezoid ABCD, AD=2BC. Express vector AD using AB=a and AC=b.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a counting formula, identity, or geometric model.
formulas: BC=AC−AB=b−a; AD=2BC.
steps: The parallel base vectors have the same direction. Hence AD=2b−2a.

problems.title: Union of square-root inequalities
problems.question: Find the union of the solution sets of √x≥x and √x≤x.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a counting formula, identity, or geometric model.
formulas: The common expression is defined exactly when x≥0.
steps: Every real pair√x, x satisfies at least one of≥ or≤. Equivalently, the individual sets are[0,1] and{0}∪[1,∞).

problems.title: Smallest positive product of trigonometric roots
problems.question: Given sinx=1/2 and cosy=1/2, find the smallest positive xy.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a counting formula, identity, or geometric model.
formulas: The smallest positive roots are x=π/6, y=π/3. The negative roots closest to 0 are −7π/6 and −π/3.
steps: A positive product needs equal signs. The least product from positive roots is π²/18; from negative roots it is 7π²/18.

problems.title: Sum of polynomial coefficients
problems.question: Find the sum of the coefficients of(2a−3b)¹⁰.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a counting formula, identity, or geometric model.
formulas: The coefficient sum is the polynomial value at a=b=1.
steps: It equals(2−3)¹⁰=1.

problems.title: A parallel section at half height
problems.question: A regular hexagonal pyramid has base side 4. A parallel plane passes through a lateral-edge midpoint. Find section are a.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a counting formula, identity, or geometric model.
formulas: The linear scale is 1/2; the are a scale is 1/4. A regular hexagon has are a(3√3/2)s².
steps: The section side is 2. Its are a is(3√3/2)·4=6√3.

problems.title: Opposite cross products
problems.question: For a=(2,1,0), b=(1,−2,3), find the cosine between a×b and b×a.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a counting formula, identity, or geometric model.
formulas: $b\times a=-(a\times b)$.
steps: The cross product is(3,−6,−5), which is nonzero. Opposite nonzero vectors for m angle 180°, whose cosine is −1.

problems.title: Choose a box before a thumbtack
problems.question: Three equally likely boxes contain red/yellow counts15/25,10/10,15/5. Find the probability of yellow.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a counting formula, identity, or geometric model.
steps: The conditional probabilities are 5/8,1/2,1/4. Their equally weighted mean is(5+4+2)/24=11/24.

problems.title: Decreasing three-digit numbers
problems.question: How many three-digit numbers have distinct digits in strictly decreasing order?
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a counting formula, identity, or geometric model.
formulas: Choose any3 distinct digits from 0,…,9. Each choice has one decreasing arrangement.
steps: The largest chosen digit is nonzero, so this always makes a three-digit number. Count=C(10,3)=120.

problems.title: Exactly four threes
problems.question: Roll a die7 times. Find the probability of exactly 4 occurrences of 3.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a counting formula, identity, or geometric model.
steps: Choose the 4 successful positions, then multiply the independent roll probabilities. Simplify35·125/6⁷=7·5⁴/6⁷.

problems.title: Points on faces of a dihedral angle
problems.question: A120° dihedral angle has perpendicular distances AA₁=a, BB₁=b to its edge, and A₁B₁=c. Find AB.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a counting formula, identity, or geometric model.
formulas: The transverse separation squared is a²+b²−2ab cos120°=a²+b²+ab.
steps: The edge-direction separation c is perpendicular to the transverse separation. Pythagoras gives AB²=a²+b²+ab+c².

problems.title: Two perpendicular equilateral faces
problems.question: Two faces of a triangular pyramid are unit equilateral triangles in perpendicular planes. Find its longest edge.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a counting formula, identity, or geometric model.
formulas: Both altitudes to the common edge have length √3/2 and the same midpoint foot.
steps: The opposite vertices are separated by √[(√3/2)²+(√3/2)²]=√6/2. All five other edges have length 1.

problems.title: Difference of sine squares
problems.question: Express sin²α−sin²β as a product.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a counting formula, identity, or geometric model.
formulas: $\sin^2\alpha-\sin^2\beta=\sin(\alpha+\beta)\sin(\alpha-\beta)$.
steps: Use sin²t=(1−cos2t)/2 and cosu−cosv=−2sin((u+v)/2)sin((u−v)/2).

problems.title: Quarter-turn points on a unit circle
problems.question: A=(cosx, sinx), B=(cos(x+π/2), sin(x+π/2)). Find AB.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a counting formula, identity, or geometric model.
formulas: B=(−sinx, cosx).
steps: AB²=(cosx+sinx)²+(sinx−cosx)²=2(sin²x+cos²x)=2.

problems.title: A tangent half-angle identity
problems.question: Find(1+sin2α)/cos2α if tan(α+45°)=6.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a counting formula, identity, or geometric model.
formulas: $\frac{1+\sin2\alpha}{\cos2\alpha}=\frac{(\sin\alpha+\cos\alpha)^2}{(\cos\alpha-\sin\alpha)(\cos\alpha+\sin\alpha)}=\tan(\alpha+45^\circ)$.
steps: The stated expression therefore equals 6.
problems.note: The identity is applied on the domain where the requested quotient is defined.

problems.title: Perpendicular diagonal sections of a pentagonal pyramid
problems.question: A pyramid has regular pentagonal base. At most how many of its5 diagonal sections can be perpendicular to the base?
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a counting formula, identity, or geometric model.
formulas: A section through an apex and base diagonal is perpendicular to the base exactly when that diagonal contains the apex’s perpendicular foot.
steps: No three pentagon diagonals are concurrent. Choose the foot at a diagonal intersection (or a vertex), where exactly 2 diagonals meet. Thus2 is attainable and maximal.

problems.title: Equal oblique segments with perpendicular projections
problems.question: AB=AC make angleα with a plane; AO is perpendicular to it and∠BOC=90°. Find cos∠BAC.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a counting formula, identity, or geometric model.
formulas: Let AB=AC=L, AO=Lsinα. The horizontal projection vectors are perpendicular.
steps: The dot product of AB and AC is AO², so cos∠BAC=AO²/L²=sin²α.

problems.title: A constant inverse-trigonometric sum
problems.question: Choose a, b from the domain of arcsinx+arccosx and c from its range. If they for m an arithmetic progression in some order, maximize min(a, b).
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a counting formula, identity, or geometric model.
formulas: The domain is[−1,1] and c=π/2>1. Thus c is the largest term.
steps: Writing u=min(a, b), v=max(a, b), we have 2v=u+π/2. Since v≤1, u≤2−π/2.
Take v=1, u=2−π/2, which both lie in the domain.

problems.title: Amplitude equals the parameter
problems.question: Find positive a for which(a−2)sinx+(a−1)cosx has range[−a, a].
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a counting formula, identity, or geometric model.
formulas: The amplitude is √[(a−2)²+(a−1)²]. Set its square equal to a².
steps: This gives a²−6a+5=0, or(a−1)(a−5)=0. Both values are positive.

problems.title: Sine levels in decreasing intervals of cosine
problems.question: Find a such that sinx=a has roots and all roots lie in decreasing intervals of cosx.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a counting formula, identity, or geometric model.
formulas: Cosine decreases on[2kπ,(2k+1)π], where sinx≥0.
steps: For0≤a≤1, all sine roots lie in those intervals. For negative a, roots lie on increasing intervals of cosine. Outside[−1,1], there are no roots.
problems.note: This uses the usual closed monotonicity intervals. If strictly negative derivative at every root were required, the endpoint a=0 would be excluded; the question asks monotonicity intervals.

problems.title: Euler’s polyhedron formula
problems.question: A polyhedron has 14 faces and 36 edges. How many vertices?
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a counting formula, identity, or geometric model.
formulas: For the usual convex polyhedron, V−E+F=2.
problems.note: Euler’s formula here uses the standard convex (sphere-type) polyhedron convention.

problems.title: Zero sum of eight vertex vectors
problems.question: For a parallelepiped, how many points O satisfy the sum of vectors from O to all 8 vertices being0?
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a counting formula, identity, or geometric model.
formulas: With vertex position vectors vᵢ and O position o, the sum isΣvᵢ−8o.
steps: It vanishes exactly when o=(Σvᵢ)/8. Opposite vertices have a common midpoint, so this point is the parallelepiped centre.
